rows.citation: Jafari F, Nadeem A (2024). Measuring Effectiveness of Metamorphic Relations for Image Processing Using Mutation Testing. Journal of Imaging 10(4):87.
rows.model_type: general image-processing software (Python Sobel edge detection, dilation and erosion programs); not a scientific simulation model
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - source-level mutants generated with MutPy mutation operators; per-operator mutant counts and kill rates reported.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - several source test cases plus follow-up inputs per metamorphic relation; inputs are images, not physical stimuli.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - compares image outputs under metamorphic relations; no electrophysiological or scientific feature extraction.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - metamorphic relations ranked by mutant fault-detection rate; no cost-constrained or greedy selection of a compact test set.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - the same mutants score relations and report results; no held-out programs or held-out mutation operator family.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-edited code studied.
rows.software: no released artifact found; uses MutPy (https://github.com/mutpy/mutpy, URL as cited in the paper)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Generic precedent for scoring tests by mutant kill rate. NeuroSem would apply this to neuron models with stimulation protocols, eFEL features, refinement-calibrated tolerances, compact battery selection and held-out models and mutation families.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.3390/jimaging10040087 (title, 2 authors, J Imaging 10(4):87, issued 2024-04-06); Europe PMC search (PMID 38667985, PMC11051087) abstract and fullTextXML read (experiment design, mutation operators, FDR tables).
rows.found_via: PubMed E-utilities 'metamorphic testing[tiab]' | Europe PMC search '"metamorphic testing" AND (simulation OR model)'

rows.citation: Masilela TAM, D-Kondo N, Shin WG, et al. (2025). TOPAS-nBio-Reg: a regression testing system for track structure simulations in TOPAS-nBio. Physics in Medicine & Biology 70(10):10NT01.
rows.model_type: Monte Carlo radiation track-structure and radiolysis chemistry simulation code (TOPAS-nBio / Geant4-DNA)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - compares real code releases (v2.0, v3.0, v4.0); no seeded faults or mutant generation.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - seven tests in paper (13 in repo) spanning physics and chemistry scenarios, e.g. several proton energies; fixed, not neuronal stimulation.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - domain quantities (LET, G-values, strand breaks) compared point-to-point as percent differences; not electrophysiology.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - developers chose tests to cover capabilities; no optimisation or selection of tests.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - version-to-version and reference-data comparison only; no held-out models or fault families.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-assisted code changes assessed.
rows.software: TOPAS-nBio-regression https://github.com/topas-nbio/TOPAS-nBio-regression (GitHub API reports no license); CI tests https://github.com/topas-nbio/qi-topas-nbio
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Scientific-simulation regression across versions using 10 seeded replicate runs and a visual 5% flag. NeuroSem would add controlled mutants, refinement-calibrated per-feature tolerances, optimised multi-protocol batteries and held-out evaluation for neuron models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1088/1361-6560/add4b9 (title, 9 authors, PMB 70(10):10NT01, issued 2025-05-16); Europe PMC search (PMID 40328284, PMC12232471) abstract; NCBI efetch PMC author-manuscript full text (seeds, 5% threshold, pass/fail CI tests); GitHub REST API repo metadata and README for topas-nbio/TOPAS-nBio-regression.
rows.found_via: PubMed E-utilities 'regression testing[tiab] AND software'; Europe PMC regression-testing query

rows.citation: Shaikh B, Smith LP, Vasilescu D, et al. (2022). BioSimulators: a central registry of simulation engines and services for recommending specific tools. Nucleic Acids Research 50(W1):W108-W114.
rows.model_type: multi-format biological simulation infrastructure (SBML, CellML, NeuroML/LEMS, BNGL etc. in COMBINE/SED-ML archives)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - validates simulator tools and projects against standards; no deliberate model fault injection found.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - test suite runs example COMBINE archives per tool; no stimulation-protocol battery for a model.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - checks that tools produce expected outputs for example archives; no electrophysiology features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - example archives chosen from tool specifications, not optimised for fault detection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - registry and service description; no held-out evaluation of detection power.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Engine-level conformance infrastructure NeuroSem could reuse for multi-simulator execution. NeuroSem targets behavioural drift of a single model after edits, using mutants, multi-protocol electrophysiology fingerprints, calibrated tolerances and battery selection.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1093/nar/gkac331 (title, author list led by Shaikh B, NAR 50(W1):W108-W114, issued 2022-05-07); Europe PMC search (PMID 35524558, PMC9252793) abstract and fullTextXML read (test suite section); GitHub REST API repo metadata and license for both repos.

rows.model_type: general scientific software (practice guidance for AI-assisted coding)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no fault injection; advises having AI write tests that catch bugs once fixed.

rows.citation: Palmblad M, Ragland JM, Neely BA (2026). Agentic AI-Assisted Coding Offers a Unique Opportunity to Instill Epistemic Grounding during Software Development. Journal of Proteome Research 25(8):4360-4366.
rows.model_type: general scientific software for mass-spectrometry proteomics (agentic AI coding guidance)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - preliminary tests use prompts that violate hard constraints; no mutants of code or models.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - not applicable; six violating prompts rather than stimulation protocols.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no test selection or optimisation.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - proof-of-principle with one model configuration; authors say false positives and planted-violation audits are untested.
rows.ai_transformations: partial - constrains agentic AI coding via GROUNDING.md and checks refusal on violating prompts; no behavioural comparison of outputs.
rows.software: proteomics GROUNDING.md draft https://github.com/OmicsGrounding/proteomics-grounding (URL as given in paper; repo not separately queried)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Preventive, prompt-level constraints on AI coding. NeuroSem is a post-hoc behavioural detector: it runs transformed neuron models under stimulus batteries and flags feature drift beyond calibrated tolerances.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1021/acs.jproteome.6c00398 (title, 3 authors, J Proteome Res 25(8):4360-4366, issued 2026-07-17); Europe PMC search (PMID 42467468, PMC13459537) abstract and fullTextXML read (preliminary testing, limitations).
